summary: @servicetitan/table preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React UI table component library but ships a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts and chmods it into a temp directory, and then invokes the dropped Bun binary against a bundled 727KB obfuscated sibling `math_init.js`. Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are heavily obfuscated (rotating string-array indirection via `WV8StW`, `_0xNNNN` identifiers, thousands of numeric constants; `math_init.js` carries `// @bun @bun-cjs` markers). A React table component library has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate language runtime at install time and use it to execute a large obfuscated bundle — this is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern that evades Node-only static analyzers, since the payload never runs under the Node interpreter the installer expects. The payload's behavior cannot be characterized because it is intentionally obfuscated and executed under a runtime outside normal Node tooling, and its execution is not gated behind any user action — it fires on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
